title: dynamic_cast
description:
Sometimes you hold a pointer to a base class and need to know whether the object is really a particular derived type. `dynamic_cast<Dog*>(animal)` checks at run time: it returns the pointer as a `Dog*`, or `nullptr` if the object is not a dog.

Write:

- `Dog* asDog(Animal* animal)`: null in gives null out;
- `int totalTricks(const std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Animal>>& animals)`: adds up `tricks()` for the dogs only (other animals have no such function).
hints: `asDog` is one line: `return dynamic_cast<Dog*>(animal);`, which gives `nullptr` for a null input or for any animal that is not a dog.
In `totalTricks`, `if (auto* dog{ dynamic_cast<const Dog*>(a.get()) }) total += dog->tricks();`.
